items.title: Anthropic is working on a system to prove AI models’ identity
items.summary: Called FlashProve, the system would let anyone check that an AI response really came from the model it claims to be from.

items.title: OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra designed a hardware device from scratch in under a week
items.summary: OpenAI's hardware team used GPT-6 Astra to design a device for the Codex coding agent in under a week, handling everything from the enclosure to the circuit board to the firmware. Several revision rounds were needed before production because the model didn't always account for manufacturing tolerances....

items.title: How “reverse game theory” could keep AI agents in check
items.summary: A new approach known as “reverse game theory” aims to control powerful AI models by designing systems that incentivize them to stick to the rules. As AI models become more capable, safety researchers are scrambling to ensure they are “aligned” with human desires—to make sure, in other words, that rogue agents don’t break the law,…

items.summary: OpenAI hires Dan Driscoll, the former civilian head of the US Army, as "Senior Counselor for National Security Modernization," likely to win government contracts and help shape AI rules for the military and intelligence agencies....

items.title: Anthropic's Message Threads cut time to first token by 35 percent for long conversations
items.summary: Anthropic released Message Threads for the Messages API. Instead of resending the entire conversation with every turn, agents now only transmit what's changed. For requests between 500,000 and one million tokens, time to first token drops by about 35 percent. The article Anthropic's Message Threads cut time to first token by 35 percent for long conversations appeared first on The Decoder .

items.title: Show HN: Modelpeers – a changelog for the AI models and agents you use
items.summary: Earlier this year, I had one of my product's features down for 48 hours because Anthropic retired Claude 3 Haiku. In another instance, an API parameter started returning errors. I grew sick of not being able to follow and track the endless changes of AI models every week, so I decided to build Modelpeers. It's basically a feed of all these changes....

items.title: New York Times and other outlets sue web browser Brave over alleged content scraping
items.summary: The New York Times is suing privacy-focused web browser company Brave for allegedly scraping the outlet’s copyrighted content and unlawfully distributing it to its own customers, like Anthropic and Perplexity.
